summary: Solid unauthenticated Prometheus probe covering the highest-value exfil surfaces: /-/reload lifecycle writes, /federate bulk metric exfil, /debug/pprof/cmdline argv leak, /api/v1/status/config with embedded scrape credentials, and /api/v1/query topology dump. All findings sit at T1 (safe-verify with deterministic 200-based signals) — the module has no post-exploitation flow, so promotion to T2 would mean actually parsing bearer tokens/basic-auth out of the config YAML into the credential store, and to T3 replaying those tokens against the disclosed scrape targets. Biggest gap: config-embedded credentials are shown but not extracted into cross-service creds; federate/pprof data is size-hinted only, never mined for secret material.

findings.tier_evidence: Version + capability-boolean summary; no vuln signal on its own.
findings.promotion_notes: Enum row; not exploitable in itself.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk http://<ip>:9090/api/v1/status/buildinfo — record version for CVE mapping.

findings.title_pattern: Prometheus lifecycle API accepts unauthenticated writes
findings.tier_evidence: POST /-/reload returned 200/204 anonymously — deterministic proof --web.enable-lifecycle is on. No payload delivered.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 would POST an attacker-controlled prometheus.yml body (or force the exposed one to reload after a config swap) and confirm scrape-target redirect via /api/v1/status/config diff. Destructive: reload alone can rotate scrape targets; /-/quit is a full outage. Gate behind --exploit.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -X POST http://<ip>:9090/-/reload; then curl -X POST http://<ip>:9090/-/quit for a monitoring blackout PoC (destructive). To exfiltrate: swap the config on disk if you have write access, then reload.

findings.tier_evidence: GET /federate with permissive matcher parsed exposition markers — content-type + '# TYPE' guard makes it deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Pull the full federation dump (unbounded), regex-scan for hostnames/service-account tokens/JWTs/env-vars-in-labels, feed to known_hostnames + credential store. Big cluster dumps are many MB — bounded fetch already exists, just needs a mining pass.

findings.tier_evidence: GET returned NUL-separated argv confirmed by NUL byte or 'prometheus' substring.
findings.promotion_notes: Pull the full argv, extract --web.config.file / --storage.tsdb.path / any *token* / *pass* flag, fold into creds. Also hit /debug/pprof/goroutine + /debug/pprof/heap for in-memory secret material (Vault-style).
findings.tester_next_step: curl http://<ip>:9090/debug/pprof/cmdline | tr '\0' '\n'; then curl http://<ip>:9090/debug/pprof/heap?debug=1 | grep -aiE 'token|password|bearer|aws_|gcp_' — mine for in-flight secrets.

findings.title_pattern: Prometheus scrape config readable without auth
findings.tier_evidence: Deterministic JSON success + 'yaml' key parse; scrape count reported.
findings.promotion_notes: Parse the YAML with a real parser (or regex fallback), extract bearer_token / basic_auth username+password / bearer_token_file references, and populate known_hostnames from scrape-target URLs + credential store. Then replay against those targets.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk http://<ip>:9090/api/v1/status/config | jq -r .data.yaml | grep -E 'bearer_token|username|password|http[s]?://' — collect creds + internal URLs, then curl each with the disclosed bearer to confirm reuse.

findings.promotion_notes: Chain queries (up, node_uname_info, kube_pod_info, process_cmdline) to build a full topology + running-service inventory as a probe payload; feeds hostnames/relays into cross-service surfaces.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sG http://<ip>:9090/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=node_uname_info' | jq '.data.result[].metric' — enumerate hostnames/kernels/architectures for target selection.
